title: Vintage Gibson SG Junior Value Guide: Prices By Year
description: SG Junior values from $2,300 to $8,500 for the original 1961 to 1971 run. Compare dog-ear and soapbar P-90 versions, cherry finishes and repairs.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Junior Value Guide
alt: Cherry Gibson SG Junior with one black dog-ear P-90 pickup, two knobs and a wraparound bridge

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Junior Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson SG Junior reference values run from $2,300 to $4,000 for later large-guard guitars to $6,000 to $8,500 for early small-guard examples, as of October 2026. These are cherry guitars with their original P-90 and finish, with the wear and maintenance noted below.

faqs.q: Can A Large-Guard Junior Have A Soapbar P-90?
faqs.a: Yes. The large-guard Junior uses a soapbar-style P-90 mounting rather than the early dog-ear arrangement. It still has one pickup and two controls.

faqs.q: Are White Or Cream SG TV Guitars Included?
faqs.a: No. The ranges here cover cherry Juniors. Cream or white SG TV instruments need their original model and finish established before a finish-specific value can be assigned.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson SG Junior Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in the condition notes. A full refinish changes the collector category, so I assess the finish work, retained parts and repairs individually instead of applying one automatic discount.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson SG Junior Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
